messages.text: I'm 4 months pregnant and live alone. I make $3,000 a month. Can I get WIC?

**Yes, you'll likely qualify for WIC.** Apply at a local health department clinic, or call 1-800-DIAL-WIC (1-800-342-5942). You can also start at https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html.

**Why it looks likely**
- WIC serves pregnant women. ([7 CFR 246.2, WIC definitions](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.2))
- WIC counts your expected baby in your household size, so your household counts as 2. ([7 CFR 246.7](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.7))
- Your income of $3,000 a month is under WIC's limit of $3,337 for 2 people. ([USDA WIC income guidelines, July 2026 to June 2027](https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926))
- The clinic will also do a short health and nutrition check.

I entered an age of 25 to run the screening, because you didn't say. That was my placeholder, not your real age. It shouldn't change the WIC result, but tell me your age if you want me to run it again.

**Other programs**
- **TennCare (health coverage): likely.** Pregnant women can qualify with income up to $4,509 a month for a household of 2. Apply at [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or call 855-259-0701. ([TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html))
- **Food assistance (SNAP): unlikely.** Your income before taxes is over the $1,729 limit for this household size. You can still apply at [OneDHS](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or call 866-311-4287. ([USDA SNAP limits](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola))

For free local help applying, dial 211.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides, and anyone can apply.

Do you already get WIC, TennCare, or SNAP? If you do, tell me and I'll check the result again.

Okay thanks. So I'm not sure if I'm already on anything. I don't have health insurance right now, and I've got about $600 in savings. My rent is $1,000 and I pay for heat/AC separately. Is there anything else I should know about WIC or TennCare?

Your results are the same after adding those details.

- **WIC: likely.** You'd still count as a household of 2 with the baby. Your income is under the limit. Savings don't matter for WIC.
- **TennCare: likely.** Not having health insurance fits with this result. Apply soon so your prenatal care is covered.
- **Food assistance (SNAP): still unlikely.** Your rent and heating/AC costs lowered your countable income. It's still over the limit, so a $600 savings balance doesn't change anything. You can still apply if you want a caseworker to look. One caveat is that the heating/cooling figure the screener used is from the most recent published numbers, which ran through 2026-09-30. Newer ones weren't available.

**Things to know about WIC**
- Go to a local health department clinic or call 1-800-DIAL-WIC (1-800-342-5942). The clinic will do a short health and nutrition check, which includes measuring your height and weight and a test for anemia. ([7 CFR 246.7](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.7))
- Federal rules say that if a pregnant woman misses her first appointment, the clinic should try to reschedule it. They can also schedule around work hours for employed applicants. Ask about this when you call.
- WIC serves pregnant women, women for up to 6 months after pregnancy (up to a year if breastfeeding), and children under 5. After your baby is born, the baby can be on WIC too. ([7 CFR 246.2](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.2))

**Things to know about TennCare**
- Apply at [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or call 855-259-0701.
- The application asks for your mailing address, phone number, Social Security number and date of birth, and money from jobs and other sources. It also asks about citizenship or immigration status, car and property value, and any other health insurance. ([How Do I Apply for TennCare?](https://www.tn.gov/tenncare/members-applicants/how-do-i-apply-for-tenncare.html))
- Newborns born to women on Medicaid are covered for one year. ([TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html))
- I didn't find anything in the policy texts about how long your own coverage lasts after the birth. Ask TennCare Connect about that.

**About whether you're already enrolled:** You said you have no health insurance, so you're probably not on TennCare. If you aren't sure about WIC or SNAP, the phone numbers above can check. Applying again isn't a problem.

**Free help:** Dial 211 for free help finding and applying for local assistance.

This is a screening, not a decision. Only the state agency decides, and anyone can apply.
